questions.prompt: The general said that if the soldiers fought bravely, they would capture the city.
questions.answer: Imperātor dīxit, sī mīlitēs fortiter pugnārent, eōs urbem captūrōs esse.

questions.prompt: He thinks that if you believe this, you are making a mistake.
questions.answer: Putat, sī hōc crēdās, tē errāre.

questions.prompt: We know that if the enemy launched an attack, the citizens would flee.
questions.answer: Scīmus, sī hostēs impetum faciant, cīvēs fugitūrōs esse.

questions.prompt: The poet declared that if he had lived longer, he would have written more.
questions.answer: Poēta dīxit, sī diūtius vīxisset, sē plūra scrīptūrum fuisse.

questions.prompt: He promised that if the storm subsided, the sailors would return home.
questions.answer: Prōmīsit, sī tempestās cōnsēdisset, nautās domum reditūrōs esse.

questions.prompt: I hear that if the river rises, the fields are flooded.
questions.answer: Audiō, sī flūmen crēscat, agrōs inundārī.

questions.prompt: The old man said that if you had hurried, you would have avoided the danger.
questions.answer: Senex dīxit, sī properāvissēs, tē perīculum vītātūrum fuisse.

questions.prompt: They believe that if the leader were present, the common people would rejoice.
questions.answer: Crēdunt, sī dux adesset, plēbem gāvīsūram esse.

questions.prompt: The messenger announced that if the gates were opened, the army would enter.
questions.answer: Nūntius nūntiāvit, sī portae aperīrentur, exercitum ingressūrum esse.

questions.prompt: He asserts that if the consul were to speak, the crowd would fall silent.
questions.answer: Affirmat, sī cōnsul loquātur, turbam tacitūram esse.

questions.prompt: We understood that if the walls had collapsed, the enemy would have taken the town.
questions.answer: Intellēxīmus, sī moenia concidissent, hostēs oppidum captūrōs fuisse.

questions.prompt: The teacher says that if the boys read carefully, they learn a great deal.
questions.answer: Magister dīcit, sī puerī dīligenter legant, eōs multa discere.

questions.prompt: The queen replied that if the gods were willing, the victory would be theirs.
questions.answer: Rēgīna respondit, sī diī vellent, victōriam suam futūram esse.

questions.prompt: I said that if you loved virtue, you would despise riches.
questions.answer: Dīxī, sī virtūtem amārēs, tē dīvitiās contemptūrum esse.

questions.prompt: He knows that if the ship is sunk, the merchants will lose everything.
questions.answer: Scit, sī nāvis mergātur, mercātōrēs omnia āmissūrōs esse.

questions.prompt: The judges decided that if the accused had confessed, they would have pardoned him.
questions.answer: Iūdicēs statuērunt, sī reus cōnfessus esset, sē eī ignōtūrōs fuisse.

questions.prompt: The philosopher teaches that if a person conquers himself, he is truly free.
questions.answer: Philosophus docet, sī quis sē vincat, eum vērē līberum esse.

questions.prompt: They reported that if the bridge were destroyed, the enemy could not cross.
questions.answer: Nūntiāvērunt, sī pōns dēlērētur, hostēs trānsīre nōn posse.

questions.prompt: The farmer swore that if it rained, the harvest would be abundant.
questions.answer: Agricola iūrāvit, sī plueret, messem ūberem futūram esse.

questions.prompt: You wrote that if the letter had arrived, you would have answered at once.
questions.answer: Scrīpsistī, sī epistula pervēnisset, tē statim respōnsūrum fuisse.

questions.prompt: The senators thought that if war broke out, the enemy would drain the treasury.
questions.answer: Senātōrēs putābant, sī bellum orīrētur, hostēs aerārium exhaustūrōs esse.

questions.prompt: He maintains that if anyone flees, he betrays his comrades.
questions.answer: Contendit, sī quis fugiat, eum sociōs prōdere.

questions.prompt: The commander warned that if they delayed, the opportunity would slip away.
questions.answer: Dux monuit, sī cūnctārentur, occāsiōnem ēlāpsūram esse.

questions.prompt: She replied that if the priest had prayed, the plague would have ceased.
questions.answer: Respondit, sī sacerdōs precātus esset, pestem cessātūram fuisse.
